target.title: Feat(senseaudio): Add SenseAudio web search provider
target.body:
<!--
Suggested PR title:
feat(senseaudio): add SenseAudio web_search provider
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Users with SenseAudio API access have no way to use it for the managed
`web_search` tool. The bundled `senseaudio` plugin only covers audio
transcription, so operators who already hold a `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY` must
configure a second, unrelated search provider (Brave, Perplexity, ...) to get
web search, even though the SenseAudio Responses API ships native `web_search`
grounding with source URLs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a SenseAudio `web_search` provider to the existing bundled `senseaudio`
plugin, following the established exa/kimi/duckduckgo provider pattern: a
shared metadata base (`src/senseaudio-web-search-provider.shared.ts`), a lazy
runtime behind `createLazyRuntimeModule`, and a light top-level
`web-search-contract-api.ts` public artifact so control-plane paths (secrets
inventory, contract registry, setup) never load runtime code. Discovery,
auto-enable, and validation are driven entirely by the manifest
(`contracts.webSearchProviders`), so no core files change.

Key behavior decisions:

- One non-streaming `POST {baseUrl}/responses` call per search with
  `tools: [{type: "web_search"}]` and a forced
  `tool_choice: {type: "web_search"}`, so answers are grounded instead of
  chat-only. Source URLs are requested explicitly via
  `include: ["web_search_call.action.sources"]`; queries are sent with
  `store: false`.
- Citations aggregate across all `web_search_call` items (live responses can
  carry more than one) plus inline `url_citation` annotations, deduplicated.
- Grounding requires a completed search call or concrete citations. A response
  whose only search call failed (or that skipped search entirely) returns a
  structured `senseaudio_web_search_ungrounded` error instead of being wrapped
  as a search result, mirroring the Kimi contract.
- Filter params (`country`, `language`, `freshness`, `date_after`,
  `date_before`) are rejected with the shared
  `buildUnsupportedSearchFilterResponse` helper like other non-filtering
  providers. There is no `count` param: SenseAudio returns one synthesized
  answer, and advertising a no-op count would be a dead model-facing arg.
- Credentials resolve from
  `plugins.entries.senseaudio.config.webSearch.apiKey` (string or SecretRef)
  with `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY` as the env fallback, reusing the scoped-credential
  contract fields; `baseUrl` and `model` (default `senseaudio-s2`) are
  overridable in the same plugin config block.

Config surface: adds the `webSearch` object (`apiKey`, `baseUrl`, `model`) to
the senseaudio plugin config schema; no new global config keys or env vars.
Auto-detection inserts SenseAudio at order 45 (between Kimi 40 and
Perplexity 50), matching the dual-use-key precedent of MiniMax (15) and
Kimi (40).

## User Impact

- `web_search` can now be backed by SenseAudio: pick it in
  `openclaw configure --section web` / onboarding, set
  `tools.web.search.provider: "senseaudio"`, or just have `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY`
  in the Gateway environment and let auto-detection select it. Results are
  AI-synthesized answers with citation URLs.
- Behavior note for existing users: `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY` previously only
  powered transcription. After this change, auto-detection (order 45) selects
  SenseAudio for `web_search` ahead of Perplexity/Firecrawl/Exa/Tavily when no
  provider is pinned. Pin `tools.web.search.provider` to keep a different
  provider.
- New docs page at `docs/tools/senseaudio-search.md`
  (https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/senseaudio-search), plus updated provider
  lists in the web-tools overview, wizard docs, FAQ, and the regenerated plugin
  inventory.

## Evidence

- Wire contract verified live against `https://api.senseaudio.cn/v1/responses`
  (three probes): forced `tool_choice` produces `web_search_call` output items
  (sometimes several per response), `include: ["web_search_call.action.sources"]`
  returns `{type: "url", url}` sources, `store: false` is accepted, and
  `annotations` stayed empty — which is why citations come from
  `action.sources`.
- Live smoke through the real provider tool path:
  `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live extensions/senseaudio/senseaudio.live.test.ts`
  passes (grounded payload, non-trivial content, citations array) in ~6s.
- Unit tests: `pnpm test extensions/senseaudio` — 16/16. Covers missing-key
  guidance, config/env credential resolution, model/baseUrl defaults and
  overrides, the exact request body contract (forced tool_choice, include,
  store/stream false), citation dedup across multiple search calls and
  annotations, ungrounded and failed-search-call structured errors, unsupported
  filter rejection, malformed/wrong-root/missing-text responses, and API
  error/status surfacing.
- Contract and loader proof: plugin registry/guardrails/loader contract suites
  pass (31/31), web-provider public-artifact fast-path and manifest contract
  tests pass, and the senseaudio registration-contract case now pins
  `webSearchProviderIds: ["senseaudio"]` like every other web-search plugin.
- Build proof: `pnpm build` succeeds; `dist/extensions/senseaudio/` contains
  `web-search-contract-api.js` (light artifact) with the runtime split into a
  separate lazy chunk (no `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT`); loading the dist
  artifact returns the provider with `createTool() === null`.
- Checks: `tsgo` core/extensions/extensions-test lanes, oxlint/oxfmt, docs
  formatting, `generate-docs-map --check`, and
  `generate-plugin-inventory-doc --check` are all green.
- Pre-PR review: an 8-angle multi-agent review with adversarial verification
  produced 10 confirmed findings (grounded-gate status check, stale generated
  plugin inventory, missing registration-contract pin, doc list coverage, test
  and code cleanups); all were fixed in this branch before submission.
